```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(SegreCP)
```

`SegreCP` implements sequential component updates on the Segre manifold. Each
update includes the preceding component updates in the same iteration. Every
tangent proposal uses the exact rank-`(1, ..., 1)` T-HOSVD retraction.

The batched decomposition path corrects contractions for preceding component
updates and refreshes the dense residual in one pass. Direct residual updates
are used near numerical precision.
Regression RGN uses the input/output structure of the tangent normal equations
to form only the blocks needed by the solver. Supplying initial components also
avoids computing an unused cross-moment.

## Two explicit profiles

The manuscript profile fixes component order and RGD step size and runs the
requested number of full iterations unless an explicit tolerance is supplied.

```{r}
segre_control(profile = "manuscript", max_iter = 20)
```

The practical profile orders components by current weight, enables a
loss-change tolerance, and uses backtracking for regression RGD. Both profiles
default to `ridge = 0`; a positive `ridge` can be supplied explicitly for
regularized RGN.

```{r}
segre_control(profile = "practical", max_iter = 20)
```

## Initializers

CPCA and HOSVD are both first-class initializers. The example below creates an
orthogonal two-component CP tensor.

```{r}
dims <- c(3, 4, 5)
factors <- lapply(dims, function(p) diag(p)[, 1:2, drop = FALSE])
truth <- cp_components(c(3, 1.5), factors)
x <- reconstruct_cp(truth)

init_cpca <- cp_initialize(x, rank = 2, method = "cpca", split = 1)
init_hosvd <- cp_initialize(x, rank = 2, method = "hosvd")

cp_relative_error(init_cpca$comps, truth)
cp_relative_error(init_hosvd$comps, truth)
```

A custom initializer can return a component list directly.

```{r}
custom_init <- function(x, rank, supplied) supplied
fit <- segre_decompose(
  x, rank = 2, method = "rgn",
  init = custom_init,
  init_args = list(supplied = truth),
  control = segre_control(max_iter = 2)
)
fit
```

For decomposition, RGN is the unit-step RGD update because the observation
operator is the identity. In regression, RGN instead solves the restricted
tangent normal equation.
